medSchoolStudLife.diversity: At NJMS, we have a long-standing commitment to fostering an inclusive environment that reflects the diversity of our community. Our mission is to develop all students with an emphasis on cultural competency, community service, and humanism in all aspects of medical education. We recognize the importance of a healthcare workforce that mirrors the diversity of our patients, as it enhances both the learning experience and the delivery of high-quality, culturally competent care. Through programs such as the Hispanic Center of Excellence, Health Careers Opportunity Program, Robert Wood Johnson Foundation/AAMC Summer Health Professions Education Program, and our Mini-Medical School, we remain dedicated to recruiting a diverse student body and improving access to care for underserved populations.

medSchoolStudLife.setting:
Located in the vibrant University Heights section of Newark, NJ—just 15 minutes from New York City—NJMS offers a dynamic environment for medical education. Newark, one of the most diverse cities in the U.S., is a hub of cultural richness and community engagement. Our campus offers innovative education and clinical training with hands-on experiences serving a broad patient demographic.

Newark's location provides easy access to Newark Liberty International Airport, connecting students to endless opportunities. Beyond academics, Newark boasts cultural gems like the NJPAC, Newark Museum, and Prudential Arena. Nature enthusiasts will enjoy Branch Brook Park, home to over 5,000 cherry blossom trees—the largest collection in the U.S.—and the annual Cherry Blossom Festival, a breathtaking event that attracts visitors nationwide.

At NJMS, you’ll receive world-class medical training while living in one of the region’s most accessible, culturally rich cities.
medSchoolStudLife.housing:
On-campus student apartments are easily accessible to school and hospital facilities. The 14-story building includes a courtyard and a parking garage. There are 234 residential apartments and a range of apartment types available for students to choose from including private studio and one-bedroom apartments, as well as shared two- and three-bedroom apartments. 
•	Several suites have special accommodations for students with disabilities
•	All rooms have wired and wireless internet access, telephone, and digital cable
•	Apartments are equipped with a full kitchen including a fridge, microwave and stove
•	Dining room table and dining chairs also provided
•	Each bedroom furnished with a desk, dresser, and closet
•	Residents in 2/3 BR units share a common living room, bathroom, and vanity area
•	Each suite equipped with seasonal central air conditioning
•	24 hour laundry facilities in the building

Off-campus housing options are available near campus or commutable from surrounding towns.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems:
At NJMS, we are committed to supporting sexual and gender minority students, as well as those whose sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, or reproductive development diverge from traditional societal, cultural, or physiological norms. We offer a range of initiatives aimed at creating an affirming environment, and enhancing the overall school community.

NJMS has developed and implemented a cultural competency training program to raise awareness of the unique challenges faced by LGBTQ individuals to foster a more inclusive campus environment, improve the institutional climate for student learning, and support students' personal and professional development.

Furthermore, Student Health Services at the Newark Health Sciences Campus provides comprehensive medical care in an LGBTQ-friendly setting, including PrEP and gender-affirming services, to ensure that all students receive the care and support they need.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: We aim to foster a culture that supports creating, maintaining, and enhancing lifestyle behaviors that will contribute to success in medical school. Housed in the Office of Student Affairs, the NJMS Circle of Wellness is dedicated to the health and well-being of all students. For more information on our wellness initiatives, please visit: https://njms.rutgers.edu/education/student_affairs/wellness.php
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture:
At NJMS, we offer more than just a medical education—we provide a close-knit, supportive community where you are valued and empowered to succeed. Our commitment to humanism in medicine ensures that compassion, respect, and humility are foundational to everything we do. You will gain hands-on experience by caring for a diverse and often underserved patient population, preparing you to be both a skilled clinician and a compassionate caregiver.

Our inclusive environment fosters collaboration, ensuring that every student feels supported and inspired to reach their full potential. At NJMS, you will not only master the science of medicine but also develop the art of caregiving, where empathy, cultural awareness, and clinical expertise go hand in hand.

Join us and become part of a community dedicated to making a lasting impact on healthcare and society. Your journey toward becoming a compassionate, well-rounded physician begins here.

medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
At NJMS, we prepare students to become skilled, collaborative physicians, educators, and researchers with a focus on improving the health of vulnerable populations. Clinical exposure starts early, giving students direct patient interaction from the first year. Our curriculum blends hands-on clinical experience with strong foundational science, preparing students to work with diverse patient populations and collaborate across specialties to address the needs of underserved communities.

The NJMS curriculum is designed with a grading system that emphasizes student development and mastery. The pre-clerkship curriculum uses a Pass/Fail grading system, while the Clerkship (clinical rotations) grading employs an Honors, High Pass, and Pass system.

In the first year, students begin with a 3-week Patient-Centered Medicine and Health Equity (PCMHE) Doctoring Course, which introduces key concepts in biostatistics and epidemiology. This course is integrated throughout Years 1 and 2 to help students develop and refine their doctoring skills.

The Foundations of Body Systems course, which follows PCMHE, is divided into two parts: Cells to Structure and Concepts in Biomedical Sciences.

Cells to Structure covers cell biology, genetics, and anatomy. Students engage in hands-on anatomy dissection throughout the course, building a solid foundation in organ systems that is reinforced in subsequent years.

Concepts in Biomedical Science introduces critical subjects such as pharmacology, physiology, microbiology, and immunology, laying the groundwork for more advanced clinical education.

This curriculum structure ensures that students receive a strong, integrated foundation in both basic and clinical sciences while honing their patient care skills early on.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: Nearly 40% of our graduates choose primary care.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms:
Over the past few years, NJMS investigators have secured over $180 million in NIH funding, reflecting steady growth in our research enterprise. Our funding supports critical clinical therapeutic needs across a range of disciplines, including cardiovascular, infectious, inflammatory, neurological, ophthalmologic, and cancer diseases. Many of our faculty members are leaders in their fields and have published in high-impact journals.

NJMS is committed to advancing biomedical knowledge and serves as a premier institution for both research and education. We aim to strengthen research resources, with a particular focus on expanding translational research programs. Our research enterprise has successfully supported a diverse array of sponsored programs, including those funded by federal, state, and private grants. The Office of Research and Sponsored Programs offers a robust infrastructure to facilitate research and related activities.

medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
Mission:
The mission of New Jersey Medical School is to educate students, physicians, and scientists to meet society’s current and future healthcare needs through patient-centered education; pioneering research; innovative clinical, rehabilitative and preventive care; and collaborative community outreach.

Vision:
To create, transmit and utilize knowledge to shape the future of medicine and to enhance the quality of life for the people of New Jersey.

Values:
-Personal respect for patients, students, staff, faculty and community
-Passionate commitment to excellence in service, research and training
-Celebration of diversity in culture, ethnicity, religion, gender and individual goals
-Professionalism in all conduct
-Commitment to serving needs of constituents
-Progress through partnerships

medSchoolInformation.programAbout: The program typically consists of three years at an affiliated undergraduate school and a four-year medical program. Although not used to determine admission, the MCAT must be taken before matriculation. Promotion to medical school is contingent upon achieving grades of B or better in all premedical courses and maintaining an overall grade point average of at least 3.5 each semester. The baccalaureate degree is awarded by the undergraduate institution upon completion of the first year of medical school. The MD degree is awarded by NJMS upon completing all NJMS degree requirements.

medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
Admissions Policy Information

We pride ourselves on cultivating a close-knit and supportive environment where students have access to outstanding clinical and research opportunities, community outreach initiatives, patient-centered learning, and student-centered support.

The mission of our admissions committee is to select talented students who are collaborative and will vigorously contribute to and care for the school community and society as a whole. In evaluating candidates, we give balanced consideration to a range of attributes such as academic excellence, lived experiences, resilience, personal growth, and maturity. Qualities of integrity, humanism, and passion are considered as these factors may influence an applicant's potential to succeed in medical school and are critical to their growth as physician-leaders.

P/F Coursework

Admissions Committee understands the challenges during the COVID pandemic and will accept P/F grades for any courses completed during that time.

Online Coursework

We will accept online courses for as long as distance learning was required and/or strongly recommended by colleges/universities as a result of the COVID pandemic.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid:
At Rutgers, Student Financial Aid programs are centrally managed and are not considered during the admissions process. Financial Aid counselors are available to meet with accepted and current students to guide them through the financial aspects of their medical education.

At NJMS, we are deeply committed to promoting Financial Literacy Education. Our Debt Management Program, held twice a year, is mandatory for first through third-year medical students. Recognizing the impact that educational debt can have on both academic performance and specialty choices, these workshops equip students with essential tools and resources to effectively manage their finances, minimize debt, and explore repayment options. In addition, fourth-year students participate in exit interviews during the winter and early spring.

To further support our students, we make every effort to secure scholarship funding through federal opportunities including the HRSA-funded Scholarship for Disadvantaged Students. Additionally, the Rutgers Biomedical Health Sciences Chancellor is matching scholarship funds up to $1 million, increasing financial support for students who are historically underrepresented backgrounds in medicine.

medSchoolPrograms.info:
3-Year Primary Care MD Program: 
     Accepted students with a strong interest in primary care are eligible to apply to the accelerated 3 year program and if accepted, receive a conditional acceptance into one of the following Rutgers-sponsored primary care residency programs: Internal Medicine, Medicine/Pediatrics (Med-Peds), OB/Gyn, Pediatrics, or Psychiatry. Program highlights include: Early Clinical Immersion, Longitudinal Primary Care Preceptorship and Health Systems and Population Health Certificate and Experiential Program. For additional information please visit: https://njms.rutgers.edu/admissions/programs_accelerated_md.php

MD with a Certificate in Population Health: 
     The 15-Credit Population Health Certificate is available only to accepted or enrolled NJMS students. This opportunity is helpful to students looking to build a foundation in public health. For additional information please visit: https://sph.rutgers.edu/academics/assets/docs/pop-health-njms.pdf

We are dedicated to providing transformative opportunities for students passionate about health professions. Our federally funded pipeline programs foster academic growth and career readiness, preparing students for success in medicine and beyond.

Our AAMC Summer Health Professions Education Program (SHPEP) is a free 6-week initiative for disadvantaged students to explore medicine, dentistry, and more, providing hands-on learning and professional guidance.

The Northeast Regional Alliance (NERA) MedPrep Scholars Program is a free, six-week enrichment program for disadvantaged students interested in medicine.

The Summer Medical Experience Scholars Program (SUMEx) is a 6-week program for EOF students, providing stipends, academic resources, and patient care experiences.

Learn more about our programs here: https://njms.rutgers.edu/education/odace/undergraduate/index.php

Join us at NJMS to enrich your academic foundation and start your healthcare career.

medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: At NJMS, we deeply value applicants who bring different perspectives, as we believe this enriches both the learning environment and the patient experience. Our longstanding commitment to a thoughtful review process reflects this philosophy. This approach encompasses a variety of factors, including but not limited to: genuine motivation for pursuing medicine and thoughtful reflection on career decisions, hands-on experience in healthcare settings, demonstrated leadership, adherence to high ethical standards, compassion for others, a broad range of extracurricular involvement, resilience in the face of challenges, and academic excellence (evidenced by GPA, course difficulty, course load, grade trends, and MCAT scores).
